extracted.intended_audience: Members and non‑Members of national securities exchanges; market participants; exchange legal/regulatory staff; interested commenters and their counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Review and evaluate an exchange's proposed rule change (fee schedule and data-product incentive) filed with the SEC under the Securities Exchange Act, focusing on statutory consistency, competitive effects, reasonableness, and procedural comment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing cites Section 6(b)(5) as the primary statutory basis and emphasizes that proposed changes should advance market integrity and investor protection. The Exchange also references the related requirement that rules not be designed to permit unfair discrimination (see 6(b)(5) language repeated elsewhere in the filing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges (Section 6(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchange rules must provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange justifies the fee change by comparing to competitor offerings, by noting a single fee will be charged per physical port even when accessing affiliated exchanges, and by explaining why the proposed $8,500/month is reasonable relative to listed competitor fees (Nasdaq, NYSE, MIAX).

rubrics_metrics.name: Not unfairly discriminatory
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules of an exchange must not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange asserts the proposed changes are equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because (for example) the discount program applies equally to all Members and non‑Members who purchase historical Open‑Close Data, and the per‑port fee applies uniformly regardless of which affiliated exchanges an access port reaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: No undue burden on competition / competitive effects analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing discusses the highly competitive environment (many registered options/equities exchanges, no single exchange with dominant share), the Commission's preference for competition over regulatory intervention, availability of substitute products, and the optional nature of the data product. It reasons that market forces and ability of participants to switch constrain supracompetitive pricing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness demonstrated by comparison to peer exchange fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the proposed fee is reasonable by comparing it to fees charged by other exchanges for analogous connectivity or data products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing cites concrete competitor fees (e.g., Nasdaq $16,500 per 10Gb Ultra fiber; NYSE $22,000 per port; MIAX Pearl $8,000 per port) and explains that even after the increase the Exchange's $8,500 fee is in line with or lower than competitor offerings. Also notes that some competitors charge per affiliated exchange while the Exchange charges once per physical port.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an industry-specific inflation index (Data PPI, NAICS 518210) to justify fee increase
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Data Processing, Hosting and Related Services Producer Price Index (Data PPI; NAICS 518210 and relevant service lines) as an appropriate measure of inflation to justify raising connectivity fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange explains why Data PPI is especially apt: it measures revenues for data processing/hosting/IT infrastructure provisioning services, is less volatile than CPI, and shows a cumulative increase (~16% since June 2018 for the Hosting/ASP/IT provisioning series). The filing references BLS methodology, PPI guidance for contract indexing, and uses a seven‑year reference period rather than year‑to‑year swings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investments, service quality improvements, and capacity increases as justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that significant investments and improvements to technology, capacity, and services support the reasonableness of a fee increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange lists specific investments (switch hardware upgrades increasing determinism and capacity by ~50%, increased network bandwidth, latency‑equalized NY6 data center add, portal transparency improvements, weekly cross‑connect audits) and argues these benefited customers and that the Exchange has not fully recouped costs of these enhancements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable and transparent terms for temporary incentive/discount programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Discount/incentive program terms should be explicit, temporally bounded, non‑combinable with other Exchange discounts, and applied equally to qualifying purchasers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the historical Open‑Close Data incentive: discount applies equally to new or current purchasers who meet the $20,000 minimum purchase (discount reduces total purchase price to the minimum once satisfied); discounts cannot be combined with other Exchange discounts (e.g., academic discount); program has stated start and end dates (April 23, 2025 through June 30, 2025) and is temporary; Exchange previously adopted same temporary program at other times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional nature of data products / purchaser choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Market data products (e.g., Open‑Close Data) are discretionary purchases and not necessary to execute trades; purchasers may choose to buy or decline based on value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing emphasizes that Open‑Close Data is optional, purchasers may request it if valuable, and the Exchange is not required to make the data available to all investors. This optional nature factors into competitive and burden‑on‑competition analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform fee application across affiliated exchanges for a single port
rubrics_metrics.description: Charge a single monthly fee per physical port regardless of how many affiliated exchanges are accessed through that port.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange notes one 10 Gb physical port can be used to access multiple affiliated exchanges and only one fee will apply per port; this is contrasted with other groups that charge separate port fees per affiliated exchange, and is used to support the reasonableness/equity of the proposed fee structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements for public comments and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear instructions for how interested persons may submit comments on the proposed rule change and how submissions will be handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing lists submission methods (Commission internet comment form, email rule‑comments@sec.gov with file number SR‑CboeBZX‑2025‑063, or paper comments in triplicate to SEC Secretary), requests use of only one method, warns against including personally identifiable information, states the Commission will post all comments on its website (subject to redaction under 5 U.S.C. 552), gives the submission deadline (on or before June 12, 2025), and notes availability of filings at the Exchange office and the Commission's Public Reference Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness and Commission suspension authority (Section 19(b)(3)(A) and Rule 19b‑4(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule change may become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) and paragraph (f) of Rule 19b‑4, but the Commission may summarily suspend the change within 60 days if necessary in the public interest or for investor protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing notes the rule change became effective under the cited statutory provisions, explains the Commission's 60‑day window to temporarily suspend and institute proceedings to determine approval or disapproval, and identifies grounds for such suspension (public interest, protection of investors, or furtherance of Act purposes).
